A detection model for positioning

Source: R/de_model.R
de_model.Rd

Wraps a range model so that the rest of the package can ask one question of it: the probability, on the logit scale, that one transmission at a given distance from a receiver is detected. The model is used as given: de_model() never fits anything, and the between-station overdispersion and the time-varying modulators are arguments the user gives.

Usage

de_model(
  x,
  sigma = list(station_hour = NA, station_day = NA),
  modulators = list(),
  blocked = 0,
  covariates = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted model, a data frame of curve values, a function or a de_model; see Details.

sigma

A list of standard deviations, in logits. station_hour is the whole spread of one receiver's logit about this curve within one hour bin. It is defined only together with the curve it was estimated around: estimate both from the same bin-scale data, and do not pair a value estimated around one curve with another (see location_surface(), Overdispersion). station_day is reserved and must be NA; the likelihood has no day-scale term. NA means not given. The values are stored for the likelihood and do not change the curve.

modulators

A named list of covariates that change with date. Each element is a constant, a vector named by receiver key, or a function of one date that returns either. de_field() evaluates them for its date and passes them to the model by name.

blocked

A logit offset added to the curve for receiver and cell pairs whose straight line meets land (in_water FALSE in water_distances()). 0, the default, reads the curve at the distance through water, as positionR 1.x did. -Inf makes a receiver deaf to the cells behind land. Range models fitted on clear lines of sight say nothing about these pairs, so the value is the user's assumption or an estimate made outside the package; it is never fitted here. Reference tags behind land can log a small share of the detections the clear-line curve predicts, so 0 can be far from right; de_field() counts the pairs it leaves at the clear-line value.

covariates

For a fitted model, an optional function that takes the data frame described above and returns the newdata the model's predict() method needs.

...

For a fitted model, further arguments to predict().

Value

An object of class de_model: a list with predict, a function of distance_m, depth_m, tag_model and ... that returns the logit, one value per element of the longest of the three (an argument of length one is recycled; other lengths that differ stop); sigma; modulators; blocked; tag_models, the tag models a table or a fitted model knows, or NULL; uses, the arguments the curve is known to read, which de_field() checks before it calls the curve; and source, one line saying where the model came from. A function that takes ..., or a fitted model given with covariates, declares only distance_m, because which other arguments it reads cannot be known in advance.

Details

x can be:

  • a fitted glm (including an mgcv gam) or glmmTMB model, called through stats::predict() on the link scale. The data frame it receives holds distance_m, depth_m, tag_model and one column per modulator; give covariates when the model was fitted on other names or units. For glmmTMB the random effects are set to zero (re.form = NA) unless ... says otherwise. glmmTMB fits the wiggly part of an s() smooth as a random effect, so re.form = NA drops it and a glmmTMB smooth over time reaches the field as a straight line. de_model() warns when a glmmTMB formula holds an s(), te(), t2() or ti() term and ... gives no re.form. Fit a smooth over time in mgcv (gam() or bam()) and pass its random-effect smooths to exclude through ...; or pass re.form = NULL, which keeps the smooth and also adds the fitted random effect of any grouping column the curve is given.

  • a data frame of curve values with distance_m and either eta (logit) or p (probability), and optionally tag_model and depth_m. Values between rows are interpolated linearly on the logit scale, in distance and then in depth. Beyond the last distance the logit continues along the slope of the last two rows when that slope is negative and is held otherwise; depth is held at the nearest tabulated depth.

  • a function of distance_m, depth_m, tag_model and ... that returns the logit. Modulator values arrive through ... by name.

  • a de_model, to replace its sigma or modulators.

See also

de_logistic() for a curve from two distances; de_field().

Examples

# The Stoney range test: hourly counts at receivers in 1 m and 25 m of water.
fit <- glm(cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m,
           family = binomial, data = stoney_range_test)
# The counts show no spread beyond binomial chance about this curve.
m <- de_model(fit, sigma = list(station_hour = 0))
m
#> <de_model> glm, cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m
#>   reads: distance_m, depth_m 
#>   sigma: station_hour 0 logits
#>   blocked line of sight: curve read at the distance through water
plogis(m$predict(distance_m = c(0, 250, 500), depth_m = 1))
#> [1] 0.95080649 0.49697702 0.04807458

# The same curve as a table of values, interpolated on the logit scale.
tab <- data.frame(distance_m = seq(0, 1600, by = 100), depth_m = 1)
tab$eta <- m$predict(tab$distance_m, depth_m = 1)
plogis(de_model(tab)$predict(c(0, 250, 500), depth_m = 1))
#> [1] 0.95080649 0.49697702 0.04807458
